sections.heading: C - New York Driver Manual Chapter One: Driver licenses
sections.markdown:
## C - New York Driver Manual Chapter One: Driver licenses

FACT_ID: sec01-F01 | anchor: A01
Legal driving here needs a valid license, a current out-of-state or foreign license is honored, nobody under sixteen may drive, new permanent residents trade in the old license within thirty days, holding two state licenses at once is generally unlawful. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=6]

FACT_ID: sec01-F02 | anchor: A01
Forging or altering any motor-vehicle document is a crime risking suspension or revocation plus prosecution toward a fine or jail. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=6]

FACT_ID: sec01-F03 | anchor: A01
Commercial licenses cover rigs rated over twenty-six thousand pounds, heavy combinations towing over ten thousand, vehicles for fifteen or more besides the driver, Article 19-A buses, and placarded hazmat loads. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=6]

FACT_ID: sec01-F04 | anchor: A01
Class D starts at eighteen, or seventeen with driver education, for vehicles to twenty-six thousand pounds, towing to ten thousand or more while the combination stays within twenty-six thousand, plus Class B and C mopeds. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=6]

FACT_ID: sec01-F05 | anchor: A01
Class DJ starts at sixteen with lower weight and tow caps under junior limits; Class E starts at eighteen, matches Class D, and adds paid carriage to fourteen passengers except Article 19-A buses. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=6]

FACT_ID: sec01-F06 | anchor: A02
Class M starts at eighteen, or seventeen with driver education, and Class MJ at sixteen, both for motorcycles and mopeds with junior limits on MJ; holding motorcycle plus another class prints both on one card such as Class DM. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=7]

FACT_ID: sec01-F07 | anchor: A02
The Enhanced license serves land and sea crossings with Canada, Mexico, Bermuda and the Caribbean as a passport substitute, works for domestic air travel, needs state residence plus United States citizenship, and also issues for commercial and motorcycle classes. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=7]

FACT_ID: sec01-F08 | anchor: A02
REAL ID is the federal standard born of the 9/11 Commission for state cards used at federal checkpoints, so domestic flyers show a REAL ID, an Enhanced license, or other federally accepted identification, obtained only at a motor-vehicle office. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=7]

FACT_ID: sec01-F09 | anchor: A02
The R endorsement for personal-use rental or recreational rigs hauling household goods starts past twenty-six thousand pounds or forty feet for Class D and E drivers, needs form MV-44 and a permit fee covering at most two road tests, a road test in matching size and type with no written test beside a supervisor twenty-one or older licensed for the rig, about fifteen minutes of turns, intersections and curb backing, then an office visit and fee. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=7]

FACT_ID: sec01-F10 | anchor: A03
First-timers file form MV-44 at any office or from the DMV website, pass vision and knowledge tests plus fees, and mostly finish a five-hour pre-licensing course and road test; the first license runs at most five years to the birth month and day with Class D, DJ, M and MJ fees set by age and birth date. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=8]

FACT_ID: sec01-F11 | anchor: A03
Applicants supply a Social Security number plus English name and age proofs from the point lists on forms MV-44.1, MV-44.1RID, ID-44 and ID-44RID; name proofs must total six points with one signed, and a current New York photo card alone is worth six points unless expired over two years. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=8]

FACT_ID: sec01-F12 | anchor: A03
Four-point proofs are DMV statements MV-45 for applicants under twenty-one, MV-45A for government-represented applicants, and MV-45B for homeless youth unusable for Enhanced or REAL ID; a valid United States passport or card; an English foreign passport with visa and entry proof or embassy-certified translation; a consular identity document; a photo foreign license; and a photo card from another United States jurisdiction or Canadian province, current or expired at most two years. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=8]

FACT_ID: sec01-F13 | anchor: A04
Three-point papers are a valid re-entry permit, refugee travel document, citizenship or naturalization certificate, unexpired resident card, valid photo work-authorization card, military photo card for active, reserve or retired members, photo benefit card, and border-crossing card. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=9]

FACT_ID: sec01-F14 | anchor: A04
Two-point papers include a military dependent card, non-photo interim license or computer permit, title, registration, Social Security card, high-school photo ID with report card or transcript, and college photo ID with transcript. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=9]

FACT_ID: sec01-F15 | anchor: A04
More two-point papers are a government marriage, divorce or name-change record, professional license, pistol permit, tribal photo card, foreign-government marriage, divorce or name-change record, benefit card without photo, foreign school record with photo, and resident or work-authorization cards expired at most two years. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=9]

FACT_ID: sec01-F16 | anchor: A04
One-point papers are a major credit card, ATM card with preprinted name and signature, canceled check with preprinted name, bank record, employee ID, pay stub showing the name, check-cashing card with preprinted name and signature, life policy in force two years, health or prescription card, utility bill with name and address, diploma or equivalency, and a W-2 showing the Social Security number. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=9]

FACT_ID: sec01-F17 | anchor: A05
The list ends with a union card, veteran access photo card, court document naming the applicant, foreign school record without photo, municipal photo ID, tax transcript or taxpayer-number letter, and Social Security statement; age is proved by one government birth certificate, state or city birth-registration certificate, military photo ID, United States passport, foreign passport with immigration papers, or citizenship or naturalization certificate. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=10]

FACT_ID: sec01-F18 | anchor: A05
Vision needs twenty-forty in at least one eye with or without correction, and failures or special lenses go to a DMV call center. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=10]

FACT_ID: sec01-F19 | anchor: A05
The Class D, M, DJ, MJ and E written test spans road rules, safe driving, signs, and alcohol and drug law, passing at fourteen of twenty including two of four sign items, with the manual's items and website quizzes as practice. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=10]

FACT_ID: sec01-F20 | anchor: A05
Motorcycle applicants also study manual MV-21MC and commercial applicants manual CDL-10 for a separate test; Class D tests run multilingual on touch screens or paper; students from fifteen years eleven months may pre-test through OKTA at participating high schools in English or Spanish with instant on-screen scoring, and schools need no driver-ed program, just a connected computer, printer and monitor. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=10]

sections.heading: C - New York Driver Manual Chapter One: Driver licenses, continued
sections.markdown:
## C - New York Driver Manual Chapter One: Driver licenses, continued

FACT_ID: sec01-F21 | anchor: A06
Online passers take a receipt, instructions and forms to any office from age sixteen to apply, and failures retake online as often as the school allows. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=11]

FACT_ID: sec01-F22 | anchor: A06
Passing vision, written and fees earns the permit, practice needs a front-seat supervisor twenty-one or older licensed for that vehicle, and under-eighteen holders follow regional graduated limits on place, time and company shown in the junior charts and leaflet MV-500H. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=11]

FACT_ID: sec01-F23 | anchor: A07
Properly licensed means licensed in-state for the driven vehicle; a guardian is a court-appointed durable stand-in parent; in loco parentis is a consented parent-role stand-in; a school course is state-approved instruction or Armed Forces training excluding zero-credit activities. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=12]

FACT_ID: sec01-F24 | anchor: A07
Junior-permit days run five morning to nine evening under a parent, guardian, in-loco-parentis adult, teacher or instructor with dual-control brakes in the city, the same list or a written designee on Long Island, while both regions ban night driving outright. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=12]

FACT_ID: sec01-F25 | anchor: A07
Upstate junior-permit days accept any supervisor twenty-one or older with a valid license, and upstate nights return to the five-person supervisor list. [A07]
Source: [A07 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=12]

FACT_ID: sec01-F26 | anchor: A08
Employment is scheduled paid work excluding driving as the job, work-study is an approved program such as credit-bearing BOCES courses, medical trips cover needed household care, and daycare trips enable family work or study; permit holders always carry a twenty-one-or-older supervisor licensed for the vehicle, a parent, guardian or instructor in the city and on Long Island, and avoid test areas, city park streets, Triborough crossings, and the Cross County, Hutchinson River, Saw Mill River and Taconic parkways. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=13]

FACT_ID: sec01-F27 | anchor: A08
Junior-permit drivers take at most one under-twenty-one passenger unless immediate family or a qualifying supervisor rides along, belt every occupant with child restraints, seat only the supervisor up front, and face added junior sanctions in the next chapter. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=13]

FACT_ID: sec01-F28 | anchor: A08
Test candidates should log fifty hours with fifteen after sunset and ten in heavier traffic, rehearse expressways beyond city streets, prefer school-based lessons, and finish an approved safe-driving course, automatic in driver education or as pre-licensing with an adult online pilot, before booking. [A08]
Source: [A08 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=13]

FACT_ID: sec01-F29 | anchor: A09
In-person course graduates present the certificate, valid one year, at booking, and the point-and-insurance crash-prevention course does not satisfy the requirement. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=14]

FACT_ID: sec01-F30 | anchor: A09
Juniors upgrade by filing the MV-285 student certificate and surrendering the junior license, or hand the permit to the examiner for automatic upgrade, else limits run to eighteen; the permit must hold valid six months first, and test day needs MV-278 or MV-285 on file, the photo permit, and a parental MV-262 certifying fifty hours with fifteen after sunset. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=14]

FACT_ID: sec01-F31 | anchor: A09
Test cars must be registered, inspected, insured, equipped and roadworthy with a clean free examiner belt, arriving drivers bring a twenty-one-or-older licensed supervisor, and motorcycle applicants supply a car, truck and driver for the examiner; other permit holders show photo permit plus MV-278 or MV-285 on file, booking online or at 1-518-402-2100. [A09]
Source: [A09 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=14]

FACT_ID: sec01-F32 | anchor: A10
Schedulers keep the MV-278 or MV-285 proof ready, weather can cancel tests with online notices, and after the drive the examiner explains result delivery while an online interim license carried beside the permit covers driving until the photo card mails in about two weeks. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=15]

FACT_ID: sec01-F33 | anchor: A10
The certified crash-prevention course, sold privately in class or online as point-and-insurance reduction, erases up to four points when eligible, repeats every eighteen months, and cuts liability and collision base rates ten percent for three years. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=15]

FACT_ID: sec01-F34 | anchor: A10
Junior-license holders take at most one non-family under-twenty-one passenger, belt all occupants with child restraints, face added sanctions in the next chapter, and follow Class DJ regional place, time and company limits. [A10]
Source: [A10 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=15]

FACT_ID: sec01-F35 | anchor: A11
Solo Nassau and Suffolk job runs, farm work included, need MV-58A employment proof, or upstate a dated signed employer letter naming business, driver, duties, schedule and a verification contact; solo school or work-study runs need a dated signed letterhead enrollment letter with official contact, activity schedule and places, and driver identity. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=16]

FACT_ID: sec01-F36 | anchor: A11
Licensed-junior days allow city solo runs only straight between home and job, work-study, college, evening high school, driver education or farm work, or accompanied by a qualifying adult, with free daytime driving on Long Island and upstate; nights ban city driving, limit Long Island solos to school and farm shuttles, and limit upstate solos to job or school runs with other night driving adult-accompanied. [A11]
Source: [A11 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=16]

FACT_ID: sec01-F37 | anchor: A12
Permit and junior motorcycle and moped riders carry no passenger but the supervisor, who holds the same-class license, stays within a quarter mile in general control, and should keep the rider visible. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=17]

FACT_ID: sec01-F38 | anchor: A12
New York permits and junior licenses work elsewhere only where allowed under local limits, so visitors check with local authorities; address changes reach the DMV within ten days by mail, form MV-232 or web with the new address inked on the license back; drivers track expiry, notices mail forty-five days ahead, missing notices mean an office visit, and renewal runs one year early. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=17]

FACT_ID: sec01-F39 | anchor: A12
Since May 3, 2023, domestic flights and secure federal sites need REAL ID, Enhanced, passport or accepted identification; REAL ID issues only in offices from October 30, 2017 against original identity, Social Security, birth-date, status and dual residence proofs plus a photo, while skipping it keeps mail or web renewal with post-2017 cards marked not for federal purposes and an eye test within six months, one year on clinical call, on form MV-619. [A12]
Source: [A12 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=17]

FACT_ID: sec01-F40 | anchor: A13
Service members keep their license through active duty plus six months after discharge on sixty-day MV-75 notice; out-of-state and foreign licensees drive until residence, then apply within thirty days. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=18]

FACT_ID: sec01-F41 | anchor: A13
New residents surrender United States or Canadian licenses with added identity proof plus vision, adding written, road and course work for short-held or long-expired licenses; other-country newcomers pass vision, course, surrender, written and road steps with the foreign card destroyed unless a written hold is filed and returned only after surrendering the New York card; young visitors obey both states' limits and nobody under sixteen drives. [A13]
Source: [A13 -> src:rdmv-ny-d:new-york-state-department-of-motor-vehic:handbook#pdf_page=18]
